deck: This week saw hefty contracts and rising interest in defense tech funding.

stories.head: SpaceX nets $4.16 billion for tracking satellites
stories.body: The Space Force awarded SpaceX $4.16 billion to develop a satellite network for airborne target tracking, reinforcing their preference for established players over competitive bidding. This contract underscores the military's reliance on SpaceX's capabilities, leaving other contenders in the dust.
stories.soWhat: When you've got the government as a loyal customer, who needs a competitive market?

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million amid defense push
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, drawing attention to its co-orbital security and space domain awareness services. This funding reflects a strong pull from the Department of Defense, as the military increasingly turns to private firms for advanced capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In defense, it seems that cash flow is now a better indicator of innovation than actual tech prowess.

stories.head: Bellatrix and TelePIX aim for air-breathing VLEO demo
stories.body: Bellatrix and TelePIX are targeting a 2028 demonstration of air-breathing very low Earth orbit (VLEO) imaging technology. This ambitious project highlights the growing interest in using atmospheric propulsion for space applications, a concept that could challenge traditional launch methods.
stories.soWhat: If this works, it could redefine how we think about getting payloads into orbit—assuming they don't run out of air first.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's next moves
watchlist.body: With a massive contract in hand, SpaceX's strategy will be crucial to watch as they balance military and commercial interests.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's growth trajectory
watchlist.body: The influx of capital could accelerate True Anomaly's development timeline, making them a key player in co-orbital security.

watchlist.title: Upcoming defense-tech IPOs
watchlist.body: As the defense-tech IPO window opens, expect a flurry of activity as companies rush to capitalize before regulatory hurdles arise.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-design review
watchlist.body: Having cleared a critical design review, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant will be under pressure to deliver on its promises in the coming months.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
